What

What Storm Cleanup & Debris Removal Involves

Storm cleanup is the post-event work that follows the immediate emergency call — the multi-day job of clearing a property once the danger has passed. It covers a property walkthrough and triage, removal of broken hanger limbs still caught in remaining canopy, bulk collection and chipping of fallen branches, full haul-off of the remaining material, and a hazard assessment of any damaged-but-standing trees with written recommendations for future work.

The distinction that matters: emergency response stabilizes the immediate danger, while cleanup restores the whole property to baseline. Roubic crews use owned chippers, saws, and sectional-dismantling rigging scaled to the debris load — most single-property cleanups wrap over one to a few days, with a final walk-through before the crew leaves.

Why

Four Reasons Homeowners Call Roubic After a Storm

The most common post-storm scenarios Roubic crews clear across NE Ohio each season.

Derecho / High-Wind Damage

Summer wind fronts scatter branches across the yard and snap canopy in mature trees. Bulk debris and hangers need clearing before they fall again.

Winter Ice Storm Loading

Ice adds weight that splits crowns and drops limbs. Rural Auburn Township properties in particular see heavy branch litter after an ice event.

Hazard Hangers Overhead

Broken limbs caught in remaining canopy over walkways and driveways are the first thing we remove — before bulk debris is even touched.

Damaged Trees Still Standing

Trees that survived the storm with structural splits or root-plate movement need a hazard assessment before the next front arrives.

How

Roubic's 4-Step Storm Cleanup Process

Every job starts with a free on-site walk. Four steps from your call to a property back at baseline. Full emergency workflow on the Storm Damage & Emergency hub.

1

Walkthrough & Triage

Lead arborist walks the property. Hazards first — hangers, leaning damaged trees — then bulk debris.

2

Hazard Mitigation

Broken hangers pulled down, leaning hazard trees removed. The property is made safe before cleanup.

3

Collect + Haul

Bulk debris collected and chipped, remaining material fully hauled off with owned equipment.

4

Assess + Walk

Damaged-but-standing trees assessed with written recommendations. Client walk-through before we leave.

Common Storm Cleanup Questions

Storm Cleanup & Debris Removal FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know after a storm.

How quickly does Roubic do storm cleanup?
Hazard work and active emergencies dispatch within 2–4 hours. Bulk cleanup typically schedules within 1–3 days after the event in Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets, depending on how much concurrent demand there is across the service area. A major weather event that hits the whole region extends the schedule for everyone.
Will my insurance pay for storm cleanup?
Cleanup of debris from a covered loss event — a tree on the house, vehicle damage, fence damage — is typically covered. Cleanup of debris that hasn't damaged a covered structure is generally a homeowner expense. Roubic provides a documentation breakdown so you can submit the covered portion to your carrier and pay the out-of-pocket portion separately.
What about damaged trees that are still standing — do they need to come down?
Maybe. Storm-damaged trees that are still standing need a hazard assessment — broken canopy, structural splits, and root-plate movement all change the future hazard profile. Roubic's lead tech walks the property and documents what we find with written recommendations for any future work.
How much does storm cleanup cost?
Storm cleanup pricing is scope-specific. Bulk debris haul-off without major hazard work typically runs $500–$3,000. Multi-day cleanup with hazard mitigation and damaged-tree work can exceed $8,000+. Insurance-coverable portions are documented separately so the split is clear.
Do you clean up everything, or just the biggest pieces?
Everything. A standard cleanup includes collecting and chipping the bulk debris and hauling off all remaining material — nothing left in your driveway or yard. If you want the wood cut to firewood lengths and stacked rather than hauled, we can do that instead at no price difference.
